title: The Life Not Taken
hook: One real fork, an ordinary day on the other side, and the desire that never quite left.
steps: Five quiet minutes. Four lines each: the fork and roughly when; an ordinary day there, no heroics; the desire still alive here; one thing in this life you would not trade.
About 4 minutes. Your partner reflects the desire in one sentence and may ask one question about that want. If it is blurry, they repeat the blur and supply no better dream.
Switch. One fork each. Close by saying keep, borrow, or leave. Borrow is a maybe for another day, not a decision tonight. Leave sets the fork down.
ending: Imagining a path is not agreeing to take it.
pass: You may pass, pause, or trade for a milder fork. The old choice is not on trial.
safety: Skip a fork that is mostly a death, an illness, or another loss. If this hides a decision that changes your partner's life, say so and pause.

title: The Unfinished Version of Me
hook: A quality you are still practicing, and a mystery you have not solved. Your partner may ask. They may not finish it.
steps: Write one of each. Still practicing: the quality, plus a recent concrete example. Clumsy counts. Still mysterious: a question about yourself you cannot yet answer.
Read them. Up to two curious questions. No diagnosis, no type, and no sentence finished for you. Advice waits until you say, "I want a suggestion."
Name one mystery you are content to leave unsolved this year. Your partner repeats it as a door they will respect. No plan and no deadline.
Switch. Both doors get named. Do not compare whose unfinishedness is more interesting.
ending: You are done when those doors have been left shut.
pass: You may pass, change a prompt, or keep a mystery at the level of a hint.

title: If Nobody Were Watching
hook: Name the audiences and send them outside. Then pursue, express, and abandon, with one ordinary line.
steps: List them and read the list: family, coworkers, friends, a former self, your partner as judge only. If one must stay, say so.
Three lines. Pursue, what you would go toward. Express, what you would let show. Abandon, what you would set down. One line should sound like a Wednesday.
Sort each item: help wanted, or mine alone. A private habit can stay a wish. If abandon would change care, money, fidelity, or safety, label it fantasy of relief or an actual request.
Your partner answers an actual request as themselves, and may take time. Then bring the audiences back. The visit is not a contract.
ending: Nothing here has to be acted out.
pass: You may pass any verb. Either of you may stop.
safety: If you do not know the label, call it a fantasy of relief for tonight and do not act on it.

title: What I Want to Experience Before I Die
hook: A personal list with Tuesday on it and the far-off hope. Witnessed, and not co-owned.
steps: Draft at least eight. At least four are ordinary or cheap. Mark grand items grand. Someday, and maybe never, still counts.
Read at human speed. A question may clarify the item. Do not turn it into a booking.
On their list, only two marks: one help you truly mean, named as a concrete offer, and one item you will leave entirely theirs.
The writer sorts: ordinary and soon, grand and maybe never, help welcome. Initial only the help you mean. No initial, no obligation.
Read one ordinary item and one maybe-never item aloud. Then stop.
ending: Hearing a wish is not a budget, a waiver, or a joint plan.
pass: You may pass, shorten the list, or leave any item unspoken. A short list is finished.
safety: If talk of dying floods you, stay with ordinary pleasures or stop. A dangerous wish does not become a plan.

title: The Questions Without Answers
hook: Six open questions. "I don't know" is a full answer.
steps: Pass as you go. Consciousness: when you are simply aware, what, if anything, is happening? Mortality: what, if anything, persists after a life ends? Love: what it is doing on a quiet day, when it is not proving itself? Morality: in a hard choice you still respect, whose good were you trying not to spend? Fate: was one choice yours, already shaped, or a mix? Mystery: what do you hope never gets fully explained? Blank, if you need one.
About 2 minutes each: a position, a fragment, or the feeling. The other person says only what they heard. No improvement. Your correction stands.
Each of you names one question to keep unfinished, and stops there. You need not agree, and you need not finish.
pass: Pass any theme, or use a plainer question of your own.
safety: Do not press a promise, a confession, or a plan. If mortality is raw, switch themes.
